summary: Source-anchored research for internalQueryMaxScansToExplode and maxScansToExplodeReached. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The ESR guide describes fewer than 201 $in elements as eligible for expansion and SORT_MERGE when used with sort, and 201 or more as range-like for following index sort fields. It explicitly warns that this boundary is not guaranteed across versions; the scan-product logic further scopes that simplified single-array rule. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/ ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

The inspected v8.0 planner multiplies point-interval counts across exploded prefix fields and sums counts across explodable nodes. Thus two eligible prefix fields of one index scan with 20 and 11 point intervals need 220 scans, exceeding a 200 limit. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

A false maxScansToExplodeReached flag does not prove SORT_MERGE eligibility: expansion can fail earlier on bounds, multikey metadata, collation, or sort compatibility. Inspect winningPlan to determine the selected sort strategy. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Lim Jong Eun's April 2024 engineering article demonstrates a three-value $in producing three IXSCAN children under SORT_MERGE, with executionStats tracing the work. Its limit discussion uses MongoDB r4.4.23 code; its experiment is independent of the vendor documentation. (low confidence)

The v8.0 threshold comparison is strictly greater-than: exactly 200 generated scans do not fail this check at the default setting; 201 do. Passing this check alone does not guarantee that the optimizer selects SORT_MERGE. (medium confidence)

Lim Jong Eun's April 2024 worked example shows a three-value $in producing three IXSCAN branches under SORT_MERGE. Its executionStats return 10 documents after examining 12 keys, illustrating the value of merging individually ordered scans when a small limit permits early termination; those counts belong to that example. (low confidence)

When the v8.0 expansion count exceeds the operation's scan limit, explodeForSort sets hitScanLimit and returns false. The inspected explain serializer exposes hitScanLimit as queryPlanner.maxScansToExplodeReached, a planning-limit Boolean rather than an execution scan counter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/explain.cpp

Raising the knob increases the permitted expansion work; it does not remove other sort-eligibility checks. The planner's own reason for the cap is that excessive index scans hurt performance. Treat a higher setting as a workload-specific experiment rather than a universal optimization. (medium confidence) Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/query_knobs.idl ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp

SERVER-83777 links inclusion of $in length in the plan-cache key to explodeForSort and caps that length at internalQueryMaxScansToExplode + 1. The ticket lists fixes in 7.0.5, 7.2.1 and 7.3.0-rc0; it concerns cache-key cardinality rather than raising the expansion cap. (low confidence)

In MongoDB v8.0, internalQueryMaxScansToExplode limits how many index scans explodeForSort may generate to obtain sort order. Its declared default is 200; the parameter accepts nonnegative integers and is settable at startup and runtime. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

Andrey Hohutkin's June 2016 report describes a compound {userId:1, action:1, time:-1} index where the product of user and action counts crossing 200 caused loss of a fast covered SORT_MERGE plan. This is a historical workload observation, not a current-version benchmark. (low confidence)

SERVER-113079 records a customer case where changing internalQueryMaxScansToExplode did not invalidate an existing cached plan, leaving nodes with different plan behavior. The ticket closed as a duplicate on June 4, 2026; this record does not establish which deployed releases retain that behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

The v8.0 planner multiplies point-interval counts across explodable prefix fields, then sums the counts across candidate index scans. Thus two eligible $in predicates with 15 distinct point bounds each can require 225 scans, exceeding the default of 200 even though neither array has 201 elements. SERVER-14034 (created 2014) describes this product threshold with a 10 x 6 = 60 scan example against the then-limit of 50; the limit was later raised to 200 and exposed as a query knob. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/v8.0/src/mongo/db/query/planner_analysis.cpp ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-14034

SERVER-130715 records promotion of internalQueryMaxScansToExplode to per-query-shape Persistent Query Settings, with resolution Fixed and fix version 9.0.0-rc1. This ticket supports a 9.0 development change; it does not establish availability of that setting on earlier server versions. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31)

A historical cnblogs getParameter listing shows internalQueryMaxScansToExplode: 200 alongside featureCompatibilityVersion: 4.0. This is historical observed parameter output, not evidence for a current server's effective setting or for the version of its binary. (low confidence)
